title: Refuge with a just king
hook: Persecuted at home, a group of Muslims fled across the sea to a Christian king.

screens.text: **Persecuted at home, a small group of Muslims crossed the sea.** They were heading for the court of a Christian king who was known for being fair.

**A just king across the sea.** He advised Muslims who had no protection to go to Abyssinia, in East Africa. Its king, the Negus (al-Najashi), was known for his justice [Qalam ep. 41; Dar al-Ifta 175].
bubbles: First a small group went, including his daughter Ruqayyah and her husband 'Uthman. Later, about a hundred more followed [Qalam ep. 41; Dar al-Ifta 175].

screens.situation: You're one of the Muslims in Abyssinia. Envoys from Makkah arrive with gifts, asking the king to send you back. The king calls you in to answer. What do you hope your spokesman does?

options.text: Tell the truth plainly, including what Muslims believe about Jesus
options.feedback: That's what happened. Ja'far spoke honestly and recited from Surah Maryam, and the king refused to hand them over.

options.text: Say whatever will please the king
options.feedback: Not quite. Ja'far didn't flatter or hide anything. Honesty is what won the king's protection.

options.text: Offer the king bigger gifts than Quraysh did
options.feedback: Not quite. They had nothing to offer but the truth, and that was enough for a just king.

screens.text: **Both sides heard.** Quraysh sent envoys with gifts to bring the Muslims back. The king didn't just take the gifts. He listened to the envoys, and then called the Muslims to hear their side [Qalam ep. 43; Dar al-Ifta 175].
A Christian king who kept his word.

events.text: Muslims with no protection go to Abyssinia, including his daughter Ruqayyah [Qalam ep. 41; Dar al-Ifta 175].

events.text: More Muslims follow, about a hundred in all [Qalam ep. 41; Dar al-Ifta 175].

events.title: Envoys from Makkah
events.text: Quraysh send gifts and ask for the Muslims back. The king hears both sides [Qalam ep. 43].

events.title: Surah Maryam
events.text: Ja'far recites from it. The king refuses to hand them over [Qalam ep. 43; Dar al-Ifta 175].

events.title: A brother's funeral
events.text: When the Negus dies, the Prophet ﷺ calls him a righteous man and prays for him [Bukhari 1245; Bukhari 3877].

screens.text: **Ja'far speaks.** Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, the Prophet's ﷺ cousin, spoke for the Muslims and recited from Surah **Maryam**, about Mary and Jesus. The king was moved and refused to hand them over, the early reports say [Qalam ep. 43; Dar al-Ifta 175].
bubbles: You met that passage on Day 27: the Qur'an's account of Maryam and the birth of **Isa** (Jesus) [Q 19:16–36].

options.feedback: Yes. Kindness and justice toward those who don't fight you over religion. That's what the Negus showed the Muslims.
Not quite. The verse says justly, alongside being righteous toward them.
Not quite. Allah loves those who act justly, and that includes openly, with your family.

screens.text: **Fairness from another faith.** When their own city turned on them, Muslims found safety with a Christian king. Goodness isn't limited to Muslims. Your Christian family and friends can be a safe harbour for you, and you for them.

screens.situation: Jordan's Christian grandmother is the one relative who has been kind since Jordan became Muslim. Someone online tells Jordan that Muslims shouldn't be close to Christians.

options.text: Keep loving and honouring Grandma; the Qur'an asks for kindness and justice to people like her
options.feedback: Yes. A Christian king protected the first Muslims, and the Prophet ﷺ honoured him [Q 60:8; Bukhari 3877].

options.text: Pull back from Grandma, just to be safe
options.feedback: Not quite. Kindness to family who don't fight you over religion is something Allah loves [Q 60:8].

options.text: Spend the night arguing with the stranger online
options.feedback: Not quite. Your time is better spent with Grandma. Questions about verses can go to your imam.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- He advised vulnerable Muslims to go to Abyssinia, whose king, the Negus (al-Najashi), was known for justice [Qalam ep. 41; Dar al-Ifta Egypt, seerah part 9].
- The first group was small (including 'Uthman and the Prophet's daughter Ruqayyah); later about a hundred went [Qalam ep. 41; Dar al-Ifta Egypt, seerah part 9]. Numbers vary; say "a small group, then about a hundred".
- Quraysh sent envoys with gifts to have them returned; the Negus heard both sides [Qalam ep. 43; Dar al-Ifta Egypt, seerah part 9]. The sources agree on 'Amr ibn al-'As but differ on the second envoy; don't name him.
- Ja'far ibn Abi Talib spoke for the Muslims and recited from Surah Maryam; the king was moved and refused to hand them over [Qalam ep. 43; Dar al-Ifta Egypt, seerah part 9]. Which verses exactly isn't fixed; the passage on Mary and Jesus is Q 19:16–36.
- When the Negus died years later, the Prophet ﷺ announced it the same day, called him a righteous man and "your brother Ashamah", and led the funeral prayer for him [Bukhari 1245; Bukhari 3877].

**Likely questions**
- *"What did Ja'far say?"* The early reports describe a speech explaining what Islam had changed in their lives. The full text is in a collection outside the six this program uses, so paraphrase it as "the early reports say" and don't quote it.
- *"Did the Negus become Muslim?"* He is understood to have accepted Islam: the Prophet ﷺ called him "your brother" and prayed the funeral prayer for him [Bukhari 3877; Bukhari 1245].
- *"Aren't Muslims told not to be friends with Christians?"* Don't quote the verse often cited for this. Teach Q 60:8: Allah doesn't forbid kindness and justice toward those who don't fight you over religion. Specific questions about a verse go to the imam. (scholar question Q19)
- *"What does Surah Maryam say about Jesus?"* Point to Day 27: his miraculous birth to Mary, his role as a prophet; respectfully, without polemics [Q 19:16–36].
- *"How do I stay close to my Christian family?"* Kindness, presence, keeping ties [Q 60:8; Q 31:14–15]; holiday questions (Q5) go to the imam; Day 14 and Day 65.

**Escalate:** holidays and religious services with Christian family (Q5; Q33 for minors); verse-specific questions about relations with Christians (Q19).

**Don't**
- Don't speak negatively of Christianity or Christians; keep it warm.
- Don't quote Ja'far's speech as a hadith.
- Don't name the second envoy.
- Don't picture the Prophet ﷺ, Ja'far or the king.
sourcesMd:

- [Bukhari 1245](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1245) (Sahih): he announced the Negus's death and led the funeral prayer.
- [Bukhari 3877](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3877) (Sahih): "a righteous man has died", "your brother Ashamah".
